results.claim: Swish containment is exactly a multiplicity-respecting directed-cycle problem.
results.proof_sketch: Let G={1,H,V,R} act on the 12 grid positions. Represent a card (p,q), after transformation g, by the arc gp→gq. In a swish, every occupied position has indegree and outdegree one, so its arcs are a disjoint union of directed simple cycles. Conversely, the cards forming any directed simple cycle constitute a swish. A component of a larger swish is itself a swish. Thus a card collection is no-swish exactly when no directed simple cycle can be formed using each physical card copy at most once.

results.claim: A no-swish collection contains at most 20 distinct transformation types, and this is sharp.
results.proof_sketch: The position orbits under G are A={(1,1),(1,3),(4,1),(4,3)}, B={(1,2),(4,2)}, C={(2,1),(2,3),(3,1),(3,3)}, and D={(2,2),(3,2)}, of sizes 4,2,4,2. There are eight internal types: three each on A,C and one each on B,D. The remaining 28 types form 14 reversal pairs {t,t*}. Using both members of a reversal pair makes a 2-card swish, so at most 14 cross-orbit types occur. On either four-point orbit, the three internal types together form a directed triangle, hence at most two occur. Each two-point orbit contributes at most one. Therefore the support has size at most 14+2+2+1+1=20. For sharpness, order A<B<C<D, take all 14 cross types directed forward, two internal types on each of A,C, and the sole internal type on each of B,D. Cross arcs strictly increase the orbit order, and the selected internal cards contain no cycle.

results.claim: Unless all eight internal types are duplicated, the usual once-or-twice interpretation of the 60-card deck already yields a 29-card no-swish subset.
results.proof_sketch: Assume, as an additional convention not supplied as a deck-specific multiplicity vector, that all 36 types occur with multiplicity one or two. Let M0 be the number of physical cards belonging to the eight internal types. Choose the six-card internal no-swish set above. For any total order of A,B,C,D, add every physical cross-orbit card directed forward in that order. The result is no-swish: internal arcs stay within one orbit, while every cross arc strictly increases the orbit order. Across the 24 orders, each cross card is forward in exactly 12, so some order selects at least ceil((60−M0)/2) cross cards. If any internal type is not duplicated, M0≤15, and the resulting set has at least 6+ceil(45/2)=29 cards. Thus only M0=16 can possibly have maximum 28 under this convention.

results.claim: The authorized input omits information essential to deciding the exact commercial-deck target.
results.proof_sketch: Start with one copy of every one of the 36 types. For Deck X, double all eight internal types and both members of eight reversal pairs, giving 60 cards. Any no-swish subset uses at most six internal cards, at most two cards from each doubled reversal pair, and at most one from each remaining pair, for at most 6+8·2+6=28; the forward-order construction attains 28. For Deck Y, fix an orbit order, double nine forward cross types, all 14 corresponding reverse types, and one internal type, again giving 60 cards. Selecting two copies of those nine forward types, one copy of each of the other five forward types, and the six safe internal cards gives a 29-card no-swish subset. Both multiplicity vectors satisfy the supplied aggregate once-or-twice data but give opposite answers. Therefore those aggregates cannot determine the answer for the actual commercial deck.

final_writeup:
The authorized material does not decide the stated commercial-deck target. It neither supplies a 29-card no-swish subset of the actual deck nor proves that every actual 29-card subset contains a swish. The resolution therefore remains PARTIAL, in agreement with the audit's VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS target judgment and ACCURATE claimed-resolution judgment.

The verified progress is structural. After independently transforming each selected card, orient it from hoop to ball. Every swish decomposes into directed simple cycles, and every such cycle is a swish, with physical copies enforcing multiplicity. The four position orbits have sizes 4,2,4,2. The 36 card types split into eight internal types and 28 cross-orbit types forming 14 reversal pairs. Local 2-cycle and triangle obstructions give the sharp bound of 20 distinct types in any no-swish collection.

Under the additional once-or-twice convention, the averaging argument is stronger: unless all eight internal types are doubled, ordering the four position orbits produces at least 29 no-swish cards. This statement remains explicitly conditional because the authorized source does not identify the commercial deck's duplicated types.

That omission is logically decisive. Deck X and Deck Y are two explicit 60-card, 36-type once-or-twice multiplicity vectors consistent with the supplied aggregate facts. Deck X has maximum no-swish size exactly 28, while Deck Y has a verified 29-card no-swish subset. Consequently the aggregate facts alone cannot select either branch of the target. Completing the target requires the actual 36-entry commercial-deck multiplicity vector, followed by a multiplicity-respecting upper-bound certificate or an explicit larger no-swish witness.
